newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine 91-day T-bill dips to 10.673 pct.
newsitem.headline: Philippine 91-day T-bill dips to 10.673 pct.

text.p: The Philippine benchmark 91-day Treasury bill rate dipped to an average of 10.673 percent at Monday's regular auction from the previous week's 10.727 percent, the Bureau of Treasury said.

This is the fourth straight week the 91-day rate has fallen since the Central Bank lowered reserve requirements by one percentage point on January 3 and a 20 percent tax was imposed on reverse repos on January 2.
The latest 91-day figure also marked a 14-month low.
But the 182-day and 364-day T-bill rates rallied.
The 182-day bill rose to an average of 11.158 percent from 11.004 the previous week; and the 364-day bill increased to 11.544 from 11.391, the Bureau of Treasury said.
The auction attracted 13.980 billion pesos worth of tenders, of which 4.5 billion pesos were accepted.
The 91-day T-bill rate garnered the most number of bids at 6.295 billion pesos, of which one billion pesos were sold.
"People still preferred the short tenors," a foreign bank dealer said, which led to the further slide of the 91-day bill.
In view of expectations that interest rates will be going up after sharply falling the past weeks, investors preferred to place their money in short-term bills, she said.
The hike in the 182-day and 364-day bills reflected the market's view the yield curve had reached bottom and started to edge upwards, traders said.
The 364-day bill had 4.465 billion pesos of tenders, of which two billion pesos were awarded.
The 182-day bills, with sales of 1.5 billion pesos, had the least number of bids worth 3.22 billion pesos.
